evidence.quote: participants assessed that the Committee was well positioned to wait for more clarity on the outlook for inflation and economic activity.
a majority of participants noted the potential for inflationary effects arising from various factors to be more persistent than they projected.
almost all participants viewing risks to inflation as tilted to the upside and risks to employment as tilted to the downside.
Almost all participants supported a slowing of the pace of runoff at this meeting.
Participants judged that labor market conditions remained broadly in balance.
a restrictive policy could be maintained for longer if inflation were to remain elevated, and policy could be eased if labor market conditions were to deteriorate or economic activity were to weaken.

parsed.rationale: The minutes convey a patient hold with two-sided risks: upside inflation from tariffs and more persistent inflation, offset by downside growth and employment risks. Slowing balance-sheet runoff leans dovish, while the inflation-persistence concern leans hawkish, leaving the net signal roughly neutral.
